Lane is frontier; no file under src/, tests/, sdk/ or pyproject.toml was created, modified or deleted (provenance.json git.untracked_paths_created_by_this_lane, git.operations_performed read-only, git.no_commit_no_push true); audit status PASS endorses the producer's MEASUREMENT_INVALID ceiling rather than a validated measurement, so PRODUCT_CORE is unavailable and SHIPPED is reserved for post-audit product promotion. Neither is emitted. Three consequences are recorded as architectural constraints and dependencies, NOT as decisions. (1) On credential-free, GET-only, stdlib-HTTP substrates at crawl hop <= 1, a capability handle that a persistent agent would replay must be treated as STALE WITHIN A SINGLE EPISODE: both observed server-minted CSRF handles differed between two GETs issued about one second apart inside each of 5 disjoint-jar sessions, so any design that persists and replays such a handle carries a structural blind cell that no threshold tuning repairs, and persistence over this object class can only amortize a PROCEDURE, never a stored handle. This sharpens and does not reverse the parent packet's conclusion. (2) For the byte-stable object class measured at hop <= 1 there is no amortization surface to buy: the 7 items whose re-derivation was measurable have re-acquisition exactly equal to re-derivation, so no finite reuse count exists for them, while the 5 remaining invariant items have NO measured re-derivation at all and must be reported as not computed rather than as infinite. Both bounds are hop <= 1, GET-only and credential-free, and say nothing about authenticated sessions, browser-mediated flows, write verbs, or sites deeper than one hop. (3) The architecture question the Global Research Director asked, whether SPIDER's persistent cross-episode state is necessary, sufficient or superfluous, remains OPEN and co-owned with product and graph; this packet supplies a constraint on it and not an answer. Token-to-latency and token-to-dollar remain explicitly UNKNOWN and were not imputed (spec.json measurement_validity.re_acquisition_cost; result.metrics.break_even_reuse_count_per_class).

THE NEXT FRONTIER QUESTION: on the same credential-free GET-only stdlib-HTTP substrate, over a frozen target pool large enough to admit state-carrying items at hop >= 3, how does the unconditional cost of obtaining ONE fresh valid instance of a state item scale with the item's shortest-path hop distance from the host root, measured in GET requests and cl100k_base tokens per item, and is that cost flat or growing? PREREGISTERED FALSIFIER, arithmetically checkable before freeze and satisfiable in BOTH directions: if the hop >= 3 median unconditional re-acquisition cost is not greater than the hop <= 1 median by a preregistered materiality factor, then fresh-instance acquisition on this substrate class is O(1) in site structure, persistent cross-episode state cannot buy a work reduction that grows with Web depth, and the honest architecture answer is that SPIDER should treat fresh-instance acquisition as a constant-cost deterministic procedure rather than an optimization target, with effort moving to procedure caching and substrate expansion; if it IS greater by more than that factor, then persistence of PATHS AND PROCEDURES rather than handles has a measurable amortization surface whose break-even reuse count can be computed for the first time from a real re-derivation cost, which is the single quantity that C-FRESHNESS staleness economics and the C-WEB-DYNAMICS timescales axis both currently lack. This Director re-verified the load-bearing findings at source rather than restating confidence. (1) THE PRIMARY METRIC IS NOT A RESULT, AND ITS MISSING POSITIVE IS NOT A NEGATIVE. The frozen falsifier could not have produced FALSIFIES for any execution: the frozen COLD_REEXPLORATION baseline is a breadth-first crawl whose route is itself a shortest path and whose token sum is a superset of the re-acquisition path's responses, so re_derivation >= re_acquisition on both units is forced by construction. Recomputed from derived/costs.json: 20 classified items have a measurable re-derivation and 20 of 20 satisfy re_derivation >= re_acquisition on both units; every one of the 7 reachable session_invariant items has re-acquisition EXACTLY equal to re-derivation, so its break-even is infinite. falsifier_triggered=false is therefore NOT support for persistence and the absent FALSIFIES is NOT a bounded negative for handle persistence. (2) THE FROZEN CONTROL GATE FIRED AS WRITTEN. raw/controls_verification.jsonl confirms KNOWN_STATIONARY_CONTROL 3 PASS / 1 FAIL / 1 UNOBSERVABLE / 1 SKIPPED and REVERIFIED_NON_STATIONARY 0 PASS / 1 FAIL / 1 UNOBSERVABLE: the prereg-named gitlab.com/users/sign_in anchor returned HTTP 403 in all 5 sessions, https://gitlab.com/explore does not exist on the page gitlab.com actually serves (it redirects to about.gitlab.com), https://httpbin.org/sitemap.xml returned 404, and both observable CSRF anchors landed in request_scoped, a class the frozen accept list EXCLUDED even though they demonstrated non-stationarity more strongly than the control anticipated. Three of four control verdicts are decided by the frozen design rather than by the Web, which is exactly why controls_pass=false maps to MEASUREMENT_INVALID and why no classification or economic number in this packet may be read as a validated scientific answer. (3) DIRECTOR CORRECTIONS TO THE PACKET'S OWN RECORD, verified at source and not flagged by producer or auditor. (a) The class-level break-even numbers are denominator artifacts: re-acquisition medians are taken over 12 and 17 items while re-derivation medians are taken over only the 7 and 13 items the bounded crawl reached, and those 5 missing invariant items are the cheap static files at 79-1923 tokens, so session_invariant reads 2 and request_scoped reads 1 while the economically meaningful item-level readings are infinite for all 7 measured invariant items and a jitter-driven 1 to 34,299 for near-identical single GETs. (b) result.observations OBS-10 and audit AUDIT-VF-05 both state that all 12 session_invariant items have re-acquisition equal to re-derivation; at source only 7 of 12 were measured, and for the other 5 the re-derivation is null with break_even_null_reason 'not computable: re_derivation unmeasured under the frozen crawl bounds'. The defensible statement is that NO invariant item has a finite measured break-even, not that all 12 are provably infinite. (c) OBS-04's claim of '5 distinct values across 5 GETs issued inside a single session' is not supported: raw/observations.jsonl contains exactly 2 requests per session, so the within-session distinct-value count is 2 in each of the 5 sessions; the substantive conclusion that these handles rotate INSIDE one episode survives, in fact it is stronger than stated, because the two intra-session requests differed in 5 of 5 sessions. (d) OBS-05's claim that https://httpbin.org/headers X-Request-Id 'produced 5 distinct values' is contradicted by the packet's own evidence: that probe's value_extract_status is 'fallback' in all 10 records with a constant value hash, and raw/controls_verification.jsonl records n_distinct_values=1 for it. The NULL_STATIONARITY_ARM's PASS is therefore carried by the /uuid probe alone (verified: 10 distinct value hashes, 5 across sessions and differing within every session, extract status ok), which satisfies the frozen criterion of at least one firing non-stationary probe, so the control verdict stands while the 'fired on both real probes' framing does not. No conclusion about header-derived request identifiers may be drawn from this packet. (e) The value-only sensitivity does not reclassify 12 items: the transition matrix computed from derived/classification.json against derived/classification_sensitivity.json is request_scoped -> request_scoped 5, request_scoped -> unclassifiable 12, session_invariant -> session_invariant 12, with the 12 leaving because the frozen five-class table has no class for 'value stable across sessions while the containing page churns' ('unmatched_by_frozen_table'). The apparent 12/5 split is a denominator shrink from 29 to 17, and result.metrics.value_only_sensitivity.n_items_that_change_class_vs_primary=6 and VN-06's 'moves 12 of 29 items' are not accurate as written. The underlying point survives and is architecturally important: the stationarity label of an item is not a property of the item, it is a property of the item AND the declared observation channel, so any agent-visible freshness guard must be channel-conditional. (4) WHAT SURVIVES, AT THE AUDITED CEILING, IS BOUNDED SUBSTRATE STATE, NOT A TAXONOMY AND NOT A PREVALENCE: over K=5 disjoint-jar sessions with a measured minimum inter-session delay of 93.81 s across 24 intervals, 29 of 32 admitted items received a class (12 session_invariant, 17 request_scoped, 3 unclassifiable, three classes zero by construction); both server-minted CSRF handles rotate within a single episode; and for the 7 measured byte-stable items re-acquisition costs exactly what re-derivation costs. 'Site' is not a stable unit here: 4 of 6 frozen roots redirect off their nominal host and 2 targets admitted zero items. (5) PROCESS FINDING, AND IT WAS AVOIDABLE. All four entries in spec.json.controls_pre_freeze_verification were PENDING with null verified_at and null evidence_ref when freeze.json existed, violating prereg sections 7 and 14. Because scripts/freeze_experiment.py hashes request.json, spec.json and prereg.md, spec.json is inside the frozen hash set, so DESIGN could have recorded verified control statuses and evidence references in the file that gets frozen. Unlike the V9/M2/M3 unsatisfiable-gate family, this defect was preventable by every actor and its prevention generalizes. (6) The packet is auditable without re-hitting the network: frozen input hashes recomputed at emit and matched (provenance.json frozen_inputs.verified_unmodified=true), 13 hashed artifact files plus 250 content-addressed response bodies under raw/responses_cache/, and no git commit, push, branch or reset operation.
